title: Here's Why BP's Partial Aker BP Stake Sale Is a Timely Move - TradingView
content: BP p.l.c. BP has completed the sale of a 5% stake in Norwegian oil and gas producer Aker BP, generating gross proceeds of about NOK 9.83 billion ($1.06 billion). The transaction, executed at NOK 311 per share, allows BP to unlock value from its investment while strengthening its financial position. Following the sale, BP retains approximately 68.7 million shares, representing a 10.9% ownership interest in Aker BP. BP’s decision to trim its stake comes at an opportune time, as Aker BP’s strong operating performance and favorable market conditions have enhanced the value of the company’s investment. By monetizing part of its stake, BP is capitalizing on these favorable conditions while maintaining exposure to Aker BP’s growth prospects. The company has agreed to a 90-day lock-up period for its remaining shares, subject to customary exemptions. The proceeds will support BP’s priority of strengthening its balance sheet and improving financial flexibility. Following the transaction, BP has raised its full-year 2026 divestment and other proceeds guidance to approximately $9 billion, up $1 billion from its previous outlook. The partial stake sale aligns with BP’s broader strategy of simplifying its portfolio, unlocking shareholder value and building a stronger financial foundation. Shell plc SHEL is pursuing portfolio optimization through strategic divestments, similar to BP’s approach to unlocking investment value. In September 2026, Shell completed the sale of its 50% non-operated interest in the Na Kika platform and its wholly owned Coulomb tieback in the Gulf of America, receiving approximately $840 million in cash proceeds. The transaction enables SHEL to streamline its upstream portfolio and concentrate resources on more competitive, higher-value opportunities. Chevron Corporation CVX is advancing its portfolio restructuring strategy through agreements to divest its ownership interests in Hess Midstream and DJ Basin crude oil midstream assets. Under the agreement, Chevron will receive $200 million in cash consideration and improved commercial terms that are expected to reduce its Bakken midstream unit costs by about 50%. The transaction, which remains subject to closing conditions, is expected to help CVX improve capital efficiency and earnings. The initiatives highlight how selective asset divestments enable energy companies to unlock value, optimize portfolios and strengthen their financial positions. BP shares have gained 23.1% over the past year compared with the industry’s 38.5% growth. From a valuation standpoint, BP trades at a trailing 12-month enterprise-value-to-EBITDA (EV/EBITDA) of 2.28X. This is lower than the broader industry average of 5.45X. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for BP's 2026 earnings has remained constant over the past seven days. BP currently carries a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy). title: Chevron's $5 Billion Gulf Oil Bet Has a Head Start - TradingView
content: Chevron CVX is closing in on a deal involving Blackstone-backed Beacon Offshore Energy that would value the operations at roughly $5 billion, the Financial Times reported. The proposed transaction would give Chevron a majority stake in Shenandoah, a deepwater oilfield off Louisiana that began producing in July 2025. Chevron has moved ahead of rival bidders, according to the FT, which reported that an agreement could be announced within days. The talks could still fall apart or another bidder could prevail. Under the terms being discussed, Blackstone would likely retain Beacon's smaller assets. Chevron, Blackstone and Quantum Capital declined to comment to the FT. Beacon is an offshore oil and gas producer that operates Shenandoah. The company said the field's first four wells reached their combined target of 100,000 barrels of oil per day in October 2025. Beacon and its partners have also approved a second phase that includes two additional wells. Chevron is already expanding in the U.S. Gulf. It credited higher output from its Ballymore, Whale and Anchor projects as a key driver of its year-over-year increase in U.S. production in the third quarter. The company has been targeting Gulf production of 300,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day by the end of 2026. If Chevron announces a deal, the terms should clarify how much it would pay, what share of Shenandoah's production it would receive and which future development costs it would take on. The field's 100,000-barrel milestone measures output from all four initial wells. title: Is Chevron Stock Overpriced Versus Its Oil Rivals? - Trefis
content: Today’s big story: Could Nvidia Stock Fall 50%? Follow The Cash Chevron (CVX) stock trades at 15.8 times earnings, the second-highest price among six oil companies in its peer group, yet three of them, all refiners, grew sales faster. The price appears to assume that Chevron will keep earning more on its sales than those refiners, and that new oil from Venezuela arrives as planned. So how much more does Chevron actually make on each dollar of sales? Chevron Keeps More Of Each Sales Dollar Than Refiners Chevron kept 14.6% of its revenue as operating profit over the four quarters ended September 30, 2026. Marathon Petroleum (MPC) kept 11.4%. Over the same four quarters, Marathon Petroleum grew revenue 31.2%, compared with 20.8% for Chevron. Yet its shares trade at just 7.7 times earnings. The extra price you pay for Chevron buys a wider margin, not faster growth. Chevron’s margin lead holds against all three refiners and against Exxon Mobil (XOM), the one peer in Chevron’s own industry. Exxon Mobil trades at 17.0 times earnings with a thinner margin, so against Exxon Mobil you pay less for more. ConocoPhillips (COP), an oil and gas producer and the one peer both cheaper and slower growing than Chevron, earned an even wider 24.7% margin across its whole company. Unlike the three refiners, Chevron produces its own oil and gas, and its plan to produce more is on track so far. In fiscal 2025, the Downstream segment, which runs the refineries, brought in $142 billion of revenue. The Upstream segment, which produces the oil and gas, brought in $88.4 billion. Chevron markets all the crude from its three Venezuela joint ventures, sending most of it to U.S. refineries such as Pascagoula and El Segundo. Management plans to double output from those ventures to roughly 600,000 barrels a day by 2031. It puts the total cost below $20 a barrel, counting both capital spending and operating costs. On the October 30, 2026 call, management said the ventures were on track for their year-end goal of around 300,000 barrels a day of gross production, up 20% over the past 12 months. Chevron’s Permian fields also topped 1 million barrels a day of oil and gas combined for a sixth straight quarter, and management plans to hold output above that level. Owning the oil as well as the refineries may be what buyers are paying for, though most of the Venezuela growth is still years away. Over the four quarters ended September 30, 2026, Chevron earned $27.0 billion in profit. It earned $22.0 billion of that total in fiscal Q2 and Q3 2026 alone. In fiscal Q1 2026, it earned just $2.21 billion. Oil traded as low as $68 and as high as $132 a barrel in the third quarter, management said, and it expects refining margins to stay elevated in the short term, with 10% of the world’s refining capacity offline. You pay about twice a refiner’s multiple for Chevron today. If its profit slips back toward its first-quarter level, that premium would buy neither faster growth nor a wider margin. Management guided a dividend of $1.78 a share for fiscal Q4 2026. It calls growing the dividend its first priority, and Chevron has done so for 39 consecutive years. So if you pay Chevron’s premium, you are betting that it keeps its margin ahead of the refiners’ and gets its Venezuela oil flowing. Over the four quarters taken together, Chevron’s margin stayed ahead of the refiners’, though its quarterly margin swung from 6.8% to 21.2%. The Venezuela growth is still mostly a plan. Chevron’s operating margin in its fiscal Q4 2026 report, expected in January 2027, is the number to watch. Neither oil prices nor project dates are in a Chevron holder’s hands. This is a good reason to spread your money across a group of strong companies rather than holding just one. title: Petrobras Stock After Q3 Earnings - Buy, Sell or Hold for Now? - The Globe and Mail
content: Brazil's state-run energy giant Petroleo Brasileiro S.A., better known as PetrobrasPBR, not only produced more oil and gas but also earned more than a year earlier in the third quarter of 2026. It also raised its annual production and cash-flow forecasts. Those are good reasons to look at the stock, even after its sharp rise this year. There are reasons for caution, too, as profit declined from the second quarter, while spending increased. For investors wondering whether to buy, the question is how much of the expected improvement is already priced in. Petrobras reported revenues of $33 billion, up 40.4% from a year earlier. Profit attributable to shareholders rose 28.4% to $7.7 billion. Excluding one-off items, profit increased 78% to $9.3 billion. Operating cash flow reached $12 billion, up 22%, while free cash flow rose 33.2% to $6.6 billion. Free cash flow measures what remains after investment spending. The stock has already rewarded investors. PBR shares have gained 54.8% in 2026 compared with 41.8% for ExxonMobil HoldingsXOM and 44.3% for ChevronCVX. A large gain alone does not tell us whether a stock is expensive, but it makes the earnings outlook worth examining closely. The results were weaker than the second quarter. Reported shareholder profit fell 25.8%, while profit excluding one-off items declined 15.9%. Lower oil prices hurt earnings, as did higher expenses. Investors should keep that comparison in mind when assessing the much stronger annual numbers. Petrobras produced a record 3.512 million barrels of oil equivalent per day (MMBOE/d) during the quarter. Refineries ran at 99% of capacity, and diesel production reached a record 769,000 barrels daily. Management now expects annual production of 3.3–3.4 MMBOE/d, up from 3.1 million. Offshore platforms are reaching higher output sooner, and the P-79 platform started earlier than planned. Petrobras also raised its operating cash-flow forecast to $45-$50 billion from $35 billion. That forecast uses higher production and revised oil-price assumptions, so the increase does not come entirely from operating improvements. ExxonMobil reported production growth in Guyana and the Permian, excluding Middle East effects, while Chevron increased capacity at existing facilities. For Petrobras, the same basic test applies: does spending lead to more production and enough cash to justify the cost? Fourth-quarter production faces scheduled maintenance and a lower Petrobras share of output under the Búzios production-sharing agreement. Investors should not assume production will rise every quarter. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for Petrobras’ 2026 earnings is $4.95 per share, up 76.8% from $2.80 in 2025. That expected increase gives the share-price rally some support. The forecast still depends on production, costs and oil prices, and it should be treated as an expectation rather than money already earned. PBR trades at a lower forward price-to-earnings ratio than its industry, ExxonMobil and Chevron. Put simply, investors pay less for each dollar of Petrobras’ expected earnings. That makes the stock worth considering after its rally. The discount needs context. Petrobras is state-controlled, which creates a risk that government priorities influence business decisions. A cheaper earnings multiple is attractive only if investors are comfortable with those risks and the earnings used to calculate it. Petrobras raised its annual cash investment forecast to $21-$22 billion from $16.9 billion. Its manageable operating expense forecast increased to $24.2–$25.5 billion from $20.2 billion. Management nevertheless expects those expenses per barrel to fall 2% from 2025. Higher lease payments also use cash. Investors comparing Petrobras with ExxonMobil and Chevron should consider how much remains for shareholders after investment and other commitments. Net debt fell to $57.8 billion. Fitch raised Petrobras’ standalone credit profile to bbb+, although its global rating remained BB. The Amapá discovery may offer future resources, but commercial development is uncertain. The agreement to buy the remaining Logum stake also awaits approvals, and its logistics benefits are expected ahead. PBR looks like a buy for investors willing to accept oil-price swings and the risks of state control. Higher production and expected earnings growth support that view, while the valuation remains below peers despite the rally. Rising spending deserves attention because higher operating cash flow does not automatically mean more money for shareholders. On balance, the price and earnings outlook favor buying over selling or waiting. Petrobras stock is currently a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy). title: Greg Abel's Berkshire Hathaway Still Holds About $18.6 Billion of Chevron Stock After Selling More Than a Third of It - The Motley Fool
content: Berkshire still holds Chevron as its sixth-largest investment in its equity portfolio. In the first quarter of 2026, Berkshire Hathaway (BRKA -1.02%) (BRKB -1.03%) sold 35% of its position in Chevron (CVX -0.47%), one of the world's largest integrated energy companies. But it increased its position by nearly 7% again in the second quarter, and left it unchanged in the third quarter. As of this writing, Berkshire still holds $18.6 billion in Chevron shares. That's equivalent to a 4.3% stake in Chevron. It accounts for 5% of Berkshire's portfolio, and it's the company's sixth-largest stock investment. Is that a bullish signal for Chevron's future? Chevron owns upstream, midstream, and downstream assets. However, it generates most of its profits from its upstream extraction business, which benefits the most from rising oil prices. It has a presence in 180 countries, but it still gets most of its oil and natural gas from the U.S., Kazakhstan, and Australia. It has less exposure to the Middle East than many of its big oil peers. Chevron expects to increase its oil and gas production by 2%-3% annually through 2030. That growth will be driven by the expansion of its Tengiz Field in Kazakhstan, drilling upgrades for its largest field in the Permian Basin, its deepwater projects in the Gulf of Mexico, and its increased exposure to Guyana, one of the world's fastest-growing oil regions, through its takeover of Hess. Chevron's stock has rallied more than 40% over the past 12 months. Most of that rally was fueled by rising oil prices after the outbreak of the Iran war in late February. However, Chevron can still easily cover its capex and dividends as long as Brent crude oil -- currently at $95 -- remains above its corporate breakeven price of $50 per barrel. That's why Chevron has raised its dividend annually for 39 consecutive years, and why it has a clear path toward achieving the 50 straight dividend hikes that would make it a Dividend King. Berkshire's new CEO, Greg Abel, was previously the CEO of Berkshire Hathaway Energy. Even though Abel isn't a celebrated stock picker like Warren Buffett, it would make sense for Abel to keep Berkshire exposed to the broader energy market through Chevron. From 2025 to 2028, analysts expect Chevron's revenue and EPS to grow at CAGRs of 5% and 26%, respectively, even if the Iran war ends and oil prices normalize. Those are stellar growth rates for a stock that trades at 14 times next year's earnings and pays a forward yield of 3.2%. That's probably why Abel kept Chevron as a top position in Berkshire's portfolio, even though it shrewdly reduced that position to more balanced levels at the beginning of the year. title: XOM, CVX, COP: This Analyst Trims Price Targets, Warns Oil Stocks May 'Struggle To Appreciate' - Stocktwits
content: Oil companies are in focus following the midterm elections and the ongoing Iran war, with energy prices fluctuating on anticipation of a deal. Meanwhile, Bernstein revised its price target on three oil majors: ExxonMobil Corp. (XOM), Chevron Corp. (CVX), and Conoco Phillips (COP) following the midterm elections. The analyst lowered the target on all three firms, saying that oil equities may struggle to appreciate. Bernstein lowered the price target on ExxonMobil to $186 from $193 and kept an ‘Outperform’ rating on the shares. The revised target implies an upside of about 9.5% from the stock’s last close. On Chevron, Bernstein cut the price target to $233 from $248 and maintained a ‘Market Perform’ rating on the shares, which suggests an upside of about 7.7%. The analyst downgraded ConocoPhillips to ‘Market Perform’ from ‘Outperform’ and slashed the price target on the company to $122, down from $129. The revised target implies a downside of nearly 13% from its last close. According to The Fly, Bernstein said that it updated its ratings and targets in the oil and gas space following the midterm elections, adding that it believes a de-escalation between the U.S. and Iran is more probable than an escalation. The analyst added that it expects oil prices to normalize. It said that it finds oil companies attractive at oil prices above $75 per barrel, but says oil equities may struggle to appreciate. The analyst also added that it is concerned about profit-taking into year-end or rotation into beaten-down sectors, and noted that it prefers gassy exploration and production companies as a result. Oil prices fell late Thursday after U.S. President Donald Trump said the U.S. does not need a deal with Iran, instead asking Vice President JD Vance to focus "his complete and total attention" on alleged crime and corruption in Democratic-run cities and states. Oil prices declined at the time of writing. Brent crude futures were trading at $95.43 a barrel, down about 0.41%, while WTI crude futures traded 0.47% lower at $88.32 per barrel. With ImmunityBio (IBRX) shares up more than 200% this year, founder Patrick Soon-Shiong has outlined plans to unveil decades of privately funded research at NantWorks over the next 12 months, spanning cancer therapies, AI chips and satellite tech. IBRX stock tumbled 9% on Thursday to $6.07, with shares down 30% for the week and tracking their worst week in nearly two years. Soon-Shiong said on X: “I began the release of our stealth, self-funded programs at Nantworks at a speech at Stanford last night.” NantWorks brings together public and private businesses across healthcare, energy and communications. Soon-Shiong highlighted an antibody search engine he likened to Google, part of an effort to find and treat tumors more precisely. He said that the search engine will use camelid antibodies to make tumors visible on PET scans, then targeting them with radioactive isotopes. The goal is to connect cancer detection with treatment directed at the tumor. He also outlined a system that gives doctors real-time patient data to help them make timely treatment decisions. Soon-Shiong said the tech already had FDA approval, but did not name the product. Meanwhile, Soon-Shiong outlined tech to move data faster as AI systems grow. These include high-speed WiGig wireless tech and optical chips that transmit data using light. He also highlighted U.S. factories to make optical chips and chipsets that connect AI data centers. NantOptiFab is already working in this area, making chips in California that use light to carry information for AI networks, space systems and quantum technology. An SEC filing in August named Soon-Shiong as a director and showed that the company raised $20 million by selling shares to one unnamed investor. His space ambitions include chips for use in space, satellite terminals that communicate using light, and new ways to build and launch satellites. The projects also extend to energy, materials and food safety. Soon-Shiong listed batteries that work in Arctic conditions, non-toxic methods of making graphene, biodegradable alternatives to plastic made from ocean-derived materials, and machine vision to detect harmful substances in food and baby food at the point of purchase. Soon-Shiong also spotlighted a blockchain-based exchange for tokenized securities, or digital versions of stocks and other investments. He pitched it as a way to give companies and investors more control. In January, Nant Global Finance announced plans to bring stock trading, shareholder records and blockchain settlement onto one platform. Its acquisitions included Horizon Globex, which provides technology for the Upstream exchange, and BlockAgent and Equity Stock Transfer, which maintain shareholder records. The company also planned to rename Arkonis Capital, a brokerage and trading platform, NantX. At the time, completing its brokerage acquisitions still required approval from the Financial Industry Regulatory Authority (FINRA). Soon-Shiong also circled back to ImmunityBio’s work on IL-15, a protein that helps activate the body’s immune defenses. Its drug Anktiva stimulates natural killer cells and T cells, which fight cancer and infections. The company is testing whether it can help patients whose immune-cell counts are too low, a condition called lymphopenia. This also includes a sepsis trial that Soon-Shiong said had been authorized. “Trials will be starting soon in USA and Europe,” he said on Wednesday. The Phase 2 study will test Anktiva in about 50 critically ill adults with sepsis and low immune-cell counts. Researchers will compare the drug plus standard care with standard care alone to see whether it reduces deaths within 28 days. “Longevity at work. Book of our patients’ stories soon,” Soon-Shiong said. The drug is already approved in the U.S. with BCG for certain bladder cancers. ImmunityBio’s approval last month expanded its use to another group of patients whose cancer had not responded to BCG. The update comes shortly after ImmunityBio’s third-quarter results, which showed that net product revenue rose 53% from a year earlier to $48.7 million. For the first nine months, it grew 92% to $143.6 million. The company also said its Quilt-2.005 trial met its main goal in a group of bladder cancer patients who had not previously received BCG. The company is on track to seek expanded FDA approval for these patients in the fourth quarter. Shares of Sellas Life Sciences (SLS) surged 17% in after-hours trading on Thursday after the company said that its key leukemia trial results are expected this month, with its CEO pointing to the treatment’s potential to become a “transformative” immunotherapy if successful. SLS stock fell nearly 5% on Thursday to $8.03, with shares on track to post their third straight weekly decline. The update is related to the Phase 3 Regal trial of Galinpepimut-S (GPS) in acute myeloid leukemia (AML). The November timeline narrows Sellas’ earlier guidance for results in the fourth quarter. “In our ongoing Phase 3 REGAL trial of GPS, we are focused on completing the final analysis following the announcement of 80th event, and we expect to announce topline primary endpoint results this month,” CEO Angelos Stergiou said. “If successful, we believe GPS could be a transformative new immunotherapy for AML patients in second complete remission.” Regal is testing GPS as a maintenance treatment for AML patients who have returned to remission after treatment for a relapse. The study’s main goal is to determine whether GPS helps these patients live longer. GPS is licensed from Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center and targets WT1, a protein found in a range of cancers. Sellas disclosed late last month that the trial had reached its prespecified 80th death, the milestone required to begin its final analysis. This process involves finalizing and reviewing the trial database, revealing treatment assignments and analyzing the results. Beyond GPS, Sellas is advancing its second leukemia drug, Tambiciclib, or SLS009, with investors looking ahead to fresh trial results and a major medical conference presentation. The company has enrolled 40 patients in its planned 80-patient Phase 2 study in newly diagnosed AML, up from 28 disclosed in August. The study includes patients whose disease stops responding early to Azacitidine and Venetoclax, an existing drug combination. Enrollment and treatment are currently continuing, with preliminary results expected in the fourth quarter. The development comes after a completed Phase 2 study in patients whose leukemia returned or failed to respond after prior Venetoclax-based treatment. Sellas will present the findings on Dec.14 at the American Society of Hematology (ASH) meeting in New Orleans. The study enrolled 62 patients and combined SLS009 with azacitidine and venetoclax. Across all doses, 34% of the 59 patients evaluated responded to treatment. At the dose of 30 milligrams twice weekly, 54% of patients with monocytic AML, a leukemia subtype, responded, with median survival of 5.8 months. Among patients with a TP53 mutation, 57% responded, with median survival of 8.8 months. Sellas ended September with $134.7 million in cash and cash equivalents, down from $138.3 million in June. “With $134.7 million in cash and cash equivalents as of September 30, we are well positioned to further advance these programs,” Stergiou said. Third-quarter (Q3) net loss widened to $10.1 million from $6.8 million a year earlier, while loss per share narrowed to $0.05 from $0.06. Meanwhile, research and development spending rose to $7 million from $4.2 million as Sellas prepared for a potential GPS approval application after Regal’s final analysis. Additionally, Sellas is preparing to study SLS009 in pancreatic cancer patients after laboratory findings presented in September. Working with the University of Wisconsin-Madison, researchers tested SLS009 in cancer models grown from patient tissue, including one resistant to Daraxonrasib. They also tested it alongside the experimental drug ZEN3694. Sellas said that the findings support further research into overcoming treatment resistance. However, patient trials are yet to begin.
